title: Univalent Non-Associative Categorical Structures
abstract: We study category-like structures in which composition is not associative, especially Munch-Maccagnoni's duploids, in univalent foundations. Included is a definition of what a univalent duploid is: one where isomorphisms of a suitable kind render the objects indistinguishable to the type theory. We show that the existing construction of a duploid from an adjunction is not univalent as a "single-sorted" duploid, and provide a novel construction which is. This work is formalized in the UniMath library for the Rocq proof assistant.

title: Comments on "Multidimensional Costas Arrays and Their Periodicity"
abstract: Rubio and Torres conjectured that a multidimensional Costas array, defined by a bijection between two boxes of integer points whose domain has at least as many dimensions as its image, can stay Costas in every window of its periodic extension only if its order is a power of two fixed by the dimension of the domain. We give a four-dimensional periodic Costas array of order $6$, with a two-dimensional domain and a two-dimensional image, so the conjecture is false. The verification reduces to $36$ windows. It has been confirmed by computer and in the Lean proof assistant. The array also meets with equality the pigeonhole bound that Rubio and Torres use for their non-existence results, so that bound is tight.
comments: Comment arXiv:2208.02378

title: On the lower bound of the refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture: proof of the cases S_{6,3} and S_{7,3} for 3x3 matrices
abstract: For Hermitian matrices $α,β$ let $\A_{n,m}(e^α,e^β)$ be the average of the traces of all words with $n$ letters $e^α$ and $m$ letters $e^β$. The refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture contains the lower bound $\A_{n,m}(e^α,e^β)\ge\Tr e^{nα+mβ}$ (Tr denotes the trace), which for $n=m=1$ is the Golden--Thompson inequality. We prove this lower bound for all $n+m\le7$ when the matrices have size at most three, and for $\min(n,m)\le2$ in every dimension. In all these cases we prove the stronger inequality $\A_{n,m}(A,B)\ge\Tr(A^{n/m}B)^m$ for positive semidefinite $A,B$, or its mirror image with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged; the lower bound of the refined conjecture follows from the Araki--Lieb--Thirring inequality. The cases with three letters $B$ in dimension three, $(n,m)=(3,3)$ and $(4,3)$, are reduced by an exact identity and the inequality of arithmetic and geometric means to a polynomial inequality in two variables, which is certified in exact rational arithmetic by Bernstein expansion on three boxes. The certificate is a short program in the ancillary files.
comments: Proof by Claude (Anthropic) checked by Gemini Opus (Google). The author guided Claude in finding the proof

title: Coinduction in Grounded Arithmetic
abstract: A grounded arithmetic counts a sentence as true only when a terminating process establishes it; a sentence no such process settles has no value. Such a logic can state that an event happens, but not that it never happens under unbounded choice. This paper extends such a logic so that it can. The base is Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) with Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA)'s least-fixed-point reading and ground induction. It adds a separate greatest-fixed-point former $ν$ with Park's coinduction rule, proves that one former cannot carry both ground induction and coinduction, and adds a dichotomy rule: the classical disjunction between a least-fixed-point atom and the greatest-fixed-point atom of its dual, under a derivable premise that the body's leaves are decided. The systems are sound for an explicit model reading every $ν$-body at its greatest fixed point, hence consistent; they agree with the least model wherever it has a value and prove sentences it leaves without one. The dichotomy replaces the underivable hypothesis that an order is well-founded by the derivable one that its steps are decided; the change of model pays for the move. With ground induction the dichotomy derives the omniscience rule of the sibling arithmetic OGA, so the system has no semantics whose certificates for universals are its own proofs. The systems prove, as single sentences, that every decided tree is well-founded or has an infinite branch given by a term, total in the new model; that random assignment terminates while its divergent twin runs forever; that a fair loop terminates and the alternating-bit protocol delivers every message; that open games are determined; that the termination gap in Nakata and Uustalu's trace semantics closes; and that Cinderella wins the bucket game at capacity three. Isabelle/HOL checks every result.
comments: 75 pages

title: A local action for Kodaira--Spencer gravity
abstract: A local action is given for Kodaira--Spencer gravity by solving a constraint on the complex structure deformation of a Calabi--Yau threefold in terms of a $(1,1)$ form as the new gravity field. The gauge algebra becomes a genuine $L_{\infty}$ algebra based on a Courant algebroid, while the gravity field and its linearized gauge transformations coincide with those of double field theory. On a real three-dimensional slice, the free action reduces to the Fierz--Pauli action for massless spin-2 plus the Kalb--Ramond action for a B-field. Non-linearly, the theory carries parity-odd interactions with three derivatives, and it is gauge invariant without a level-matching constraint, in this sense defining an unconstrained double field theory. The full theory is encoded in a cyclic $L_{\infty}$ algebra, for which a double copy interpretation is given.
comments: 28 pages, produced in collaboration with Claude

title: Promotion and Extension of General Escape-Covering Duality Relationship
abstract: Bellman's lost-in-a-forest problem, Moser's worm problem, Lebesgue's universal covering problems, and the classical 'fits and covers' questions can be organized by a common obstruction principle: an object fits a region if some admissible group action places it in the region, whereas an escape object is one for which every placement fails to remain in the interior. In this paper, we develop a general theory of escape-covering duality for any dimension and explore several applications. For convex translation covers of all closed planar curves of Euclidean length one, we prove $ W \ge f(\sqrt3/9)+c_1>0.15545785378555,c_1=0.000009944944227372... $ Here $f(\sqrt3/9)$ is Wetzel's classical lower bound. For a rational polytopal Minkowski gauge and prescribed rational facet directions, we express universal closed-loop cover feasibility as a rational polyhedron in the facet offsets. After removing translations, minimum volume is attained at a vertex. Refining the facet directions gives explicit two-sided rational bounds for the unrestricted fixed-gauge worm constant. Four exact benchmarks recover known sharp values. The construction uses an elementary circuit--circumradius form of the established non-fitting-polygon and capacity theory. We supply its support and ledger derivation, the finite complete test family in arbitrary dimension, a cover vertex bound, and the resulting algebraicity statement. The surrounding escape--covering framework includes endpoint placement, attainment, gauge stability, and finite-to-continuum error bounds. For nonsymmetric gauges the objects are parametrized closed curves, so orientation-dependent length is retained. Through the published capacity identity, the improved Wetzel estimate gives a product volume--capacity factor below $1.023781939711102$ for every planar ellipsoidal gauge.
comments: 83 pages including formalized proofs in Lean

title: Conic Certification of Transformer Attention
abstract: Attention is the computational core of large language models, yet the verifiers that bound how far an attention head's output can move under input perturbations give no guarantee on how loose their bounds are. A weak certificate therefore cannot be told apart from a fragile model. We develop a conic programming theory of attention certification that supplies this guarantee. We prove that the difficulty lies not in the softmax but in the bilinear interaction of a varying query with the keys. This interaction makes certification NP-hard over boxes and inapproximable once the attention logits can move by a constant amount. A fixed query or listed token substitutions, by contrast, make the exact worst case efficiently computable. An exponential cone moment relaxation then certifies a head with an error bounded quadratically in the perturbation radius by computable quantities, an order that cannot be improved. We also show that relaxations that treat a network one operation at a time, linear bound propagation among them, pay on second-order terms a sum of per-operation maxima instead of one coupled maximum. Computational results on GPT-2 indicate that the theory carries over to a trained model. Against exact worst cases with the query fixed, the certificate attains the predicted second-order accuracy. It is tighter than linear bound propagation on every head, and the looseness of bound propagation tracks the predicted per-operation excess.
comments: 56 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/chimera1001/conic-attention-cert

title: Log-Driven Semantic Tuning for Mixed Integer Programming Solvers
abstract: Automated configuration of mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers largely relies on black-box optimization. Each trial requires an expensive solver run and provides only a scalar outcome, so tuning can require many such evaluations. Human experts take a different approach. They inspect solver logs, identify performance bottlenecks, and adjust the parameters that address them. We propose Log-Driven Semantic Tuning (LDST), which uses a large language model (LLM) to automate this process. LDST extracts compact diagnostics from solver logs, uses the LLM to propose sparse edits to the current best configuration based on parameter meanings and observed solver behavior, and validates each proposal before execution. A regime-adaptive objective selects the tuning signal according to the information available from a time-limited run, while a log-based completion signal estimates completion time from branch-and-bound tree growth recorded in ordinary solver logs, so that solved and unsolved runs share one time scale. On 215 instances from five benchmark sets, LDST reduces geometric-mean loss by 43.9% on easy instances and 16.7% on intermediate instances relative to the best of SMAC3, RBFOpt, and random search. In both regimes, LDST achieves a lower loss with 10 proposals than any of these baselines achieves with 50. Configurations that LDST tunes on a single instance also transfer better than baseline configurations to unseen instances of the same family.
comments: 34 pages, 8 figures, 28 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/Zhengzhong-You/LDST

title: Agent4FreeFem: A Verification-Guided Framework for Autonomous Topology Optimization
abstract: Topology optimization has become an indispensable design tool in the aerospace, automotive, and mechanical engineering industries. Yet bringing a new problem from its description to an optimized result remains slow, expert-dependent, and unreliable: the workflow spans many manually connected stages, each new problem requires solver code to be written and debugged manually, and such code often fails or yields incorrect results. We present Agent4FreeFem, a pipeline driven by a large language model that turns a natural-language problem description into a set of verified optimization results without manual solver-code development or debugging. The pipeline keeps the problem definition unmodified, localizes errors using independent sources of evidence, and completes constrained repairs automatically, thereby providing efficient end-to-end automation, autonomous execution, and verifiable results. We evaluated Agent4FreeFem on a suite of single-physics and coupled multiphysics problems. Every case passed runtime verification and finished within the repair budget of each stage.
comments: 23 pages, 10 figures, 8 tables

title: Twisting-free converse theorems for $Γ_0(32)$ and $Γ_0(36)$
abstract: We prove twisting-free converse theorems for $Γ_0(32)$ and $Γ_0(36)$ under the setting of Conrey--Farmer, namely assuming a single functional equation and a suitable Euler product, with particular shapes at ramified primes. The proofs make substantial use of the ramified primes, with methods somewhat different from the existing ones in the literature.
comments: This paper has 8 pages. The original proof was generated by GPT, while the paper itself was written solely by the author according to his own understanding. The author takes full responsibility for the correctness of this paper

title: The Golden Quadruple: Four Reals Whose Differences Form a Geometric Progression, Rigidity of the Golden Ratio, and a Bohr Almost Periodic Cosine Sum
abstract: Let $φ=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. The four-point set $\{0,φ,φ^2,φ^3\}$ is classical: up to a dilation it consists of the two endpoints and the two crossing points on a side of the regular pentagram (Euclid, Elements XIII.8), and, by the identity $φ^2=φ+1$, its six pairwise differences are $1,φ,φ^2,φ^3$, with multiplicities $1,2,2,1$. We write this configuration as the golden quadruple $S=(F, F-a, F-b, F-a-b)$, where $u>0$, $a=φu$, $b=φ^2u$ and $F>a+b$, and study its extremal and rigidity properties. We prove that it is maximal and unique: no five distinct real numbers have all their positive differences in $\{u,φu,φ^2u,φ^3u\}$ (indeed, not even in the whole set $\{uφ^n:n\in\mathbb{Z}\}$), and every four-element set with this property is a translate of $S$. We prove that the golden ratio is forced: $φ$ is the only ratio $x>1$ for which some four-point set of reals has the four-term progression $\{c,cx,cx^2,cx^3\}$ as its set of distinct differences. For the analogous quadruple with base $x>1$, $x\neqφ$, the failure is measured by two closure residues, $(x^2-x-1)u$ and $x(x^2-x-1)u$, which along Fibonacci quotients equal $\pm u/F_n^2$ and $\pm F_{n+1}u/F_n^3$. Finally, the cosine sum $C_S(t)=\sum\cos(2πd t)$ over the six differences equals $8\cos^2(πa t)\cos^2(πb t)-2$; it is not periodic, but it is almost periodic in the sense of Bohr, with explicit almost periods $F_n/u$. For an arbitrary scale $K>0$ the golden ladder $ν_n=Kφ^{-n}$ realises the construction with $u=ν_{203}$, so that the differences are $ν_{200},\dots,ν_{203}$; we evaluate it for $K=\sqrt{c^5/(Gh)}$. We state explicitly what is classical and what is new, in relation to difference sets, Golomb rulers, Sidon sets, Fibonacci numbers, quasicrystals and almost periodic functions.
comments: 23 pages. Lean 4 formalization and Polish version: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23798809

title: Magnetic norm inflation below the velocity regularity threshold for viscous non-resistive MHD
abstract: We study viscous, non-resistive magnetohydrodynamics on $\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$. For every fixed magnetic exponent $s>d/2$ and every velocity exponent $q<s-1$, we prove norm inflation at the origin in $H^q\times H^s$. Arbitrarily small divergence-free Schwartz data generate classical solutions whose magnetic $H^s$ norm becomes arbitrarily large at arbitrarily small positive times, while the velocity remains arbitrarily small in $H^q$ throughout the observation interval. Together with endpoint local well-posedness, this identifies $q=s-1$ as the sharp lower velocity threshold for fixed $s>d/2$. The construction uses a symmetric pair of high-frequency velocity packets and a fixed low-frequency magnetic profile. A Fourier component of their stretching interaction has a fixed sign and gains the power $K^{s-1-q}$ on a short diffusive time scale. Subtracting an exact reference flow and using endpoint Besov estimates controls the full nonlinear remainder. Quantitative higher-order estimates ensure existence through the observation time and yield the uniform smallness of the velocity in the target norm.
comments: This is a readable PDE research paper generated by ChatGPT under the author's guidance

title: An $\mathsf{FPRAS}$ for Mixed Volumes
abstract: We design the first fully polynomial-time randomized approximation scheme ($\mathsf{FPRAS}$) to estimate the mixed volume of $n$ arbitrary compact convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ specified by weak membership oracles. This disproves a longstanding conjecture of Gurvits (2009). $\textbf{AI Disclosure}$ The main ideas were generated entirely by GPT 6 Astra. The purpose of this paper is to provide a human-written exposition of the algorithm.

title: The classification of Fano contact manifolds revisited
abstract: We present an account of the classification of Fano contact manifolds based on the proof of OpenAI and the solution of LeBrun-Salamon conjecture by Hu, Liu and Wan. The proof combines their constructions with earlier results on contact lines, with some simplifications.
comments: This paper grew out from my attemps to understand [OpenAI] and [HLW] through extensive discussions with ChatGPT. My contribution is mainly editorial: the rewriting, reformulation and reorganization of claims and proofs; the explanation and illustration of the proof via adjoint varieties (which is the essential part of my contribution in this paper); attributions of previous works etc

title: Short Paper No. 1: Relation between integer sequence A319433 and the maximum degrees of finite linear Jaco graphs
abstract: This short paper presents the interesting relation between integer sequence A319433 in https://oeis.org and the maximum degrees of the family of finite linear Jaco graphs $J_n(x)$ where $n = 1,2,3,\dots$. The result first appeared as a conjecture. Subsequently, a proof through AI-assisted mathematical reasoning came to the fore. Appropriate clarity remarks follow in the main text. It appears that $\textit{Golden ratio}$-like floor function plays an important role in the analysis of the graph structural properties of the family of finite linear Jaco graphs.
comments: 8 pages

title: A log-concavity criterion for finite nonnegative linearization
abstract: In a 2005 survey, R. Szwarc asked for criteria, stated in the recurrence coefficients, for nonnegative linearization (property (P)) of finite orthogonal polynomial systems such as the Krawtchouk polynomials. For a finite three-term recurrence normalized to have row sums one, whose diagonal and downward coefficients have a constant nonnegative ratio, we prove that property (P) holds for every product, including products beyond the terminal degree, whenever the Newton coefficients of the profile $d_i=b_i+c_i$ are log-concave without internal zeros. The criterion contains the full positive Krawtchouk range and the dual $q$-Krawtchouk arrays, and through a quadratic decomposition of symmetric finite systems it covers Szwarc's quadratic system $Q_n$ in its sharp range $0<p_0\leq1/2$. As a limit to any such criterion, property (P) fails at coefficient distance $O((1-r^2)^N)$ from the Krawtchouk array of size $N$ with fixed ratio $c_i/d_i=r<1$. All theorems, corollaries and propositions are formalized in Lean 4.
comments: 21 pages. Lean 4 formalization and exact diagnostics at https://github.com/skypher/szkraw

title: A proof of the sharpness conjectures for all saturated fusion systems
abstract: We prove the Díaz$\unicode[Arial]{x2013}$Park conjecture for sharpness of saturated fusion systems. More generally, for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over the localisation $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of the integers at $p$, the higher limits of its contravariant part over the centric orbit category vanish in all positive degrees. In particular, the subgroup and normaliser decompositions of every $p$-local finite group $(S,\mathcal F,\mathcal L)$ over the $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups are sharp. This answers in the affirmative a question in the list of important open problems in [M. Aschbacher, R. Kessar and B. Oliver, Fusion Systems in Algebra and Topology, Cambridge Univ. Press (2011)], and proves the sharpness conjecture stated in [M. Aschbacher and B. Oliver, Fusion systems, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (2016)] and Conjecture 1.2 of [E. Yalç$\unicode[Arial]{x131}$n, Higher limits over the fusion orbit category, Adv. Math. (2022)]. The proof is algebraic and does not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.
comments: Lean and Rocq unconditional formalisations (about 62,000 and 100,000 lines of project source). Compilation on personal laptop took about 2.7 hours for Lean under Windows and 3.4 hours for Rocq under Linux. There is a report that describes the details of the formalisations and the underlying theories. See the acknowledgemets for more details

title: Nonreciprocal Spherical Attention and Retrieval: Sharp Coarsening Clocks and Certified Score Correction
abstract: We develop nonreciprocal spherical attention as a mathematical framework for coarsening and compressed nearest-neighbor retrieval. For two shrinking acute blocks whose centers have zero skew pairing and whose total mass ratio is subexponential in inverse temperature, we prove $\lim_{β\to\infty}β^{-1}\log T_β=1-\cosϕ$, without restricting particle-count growth. An explicit three-body flow has two rigorously separated metastable exponents. For finite compression, mass centering yields a sharp $O(r^2)$ attention-output error bound at fixed temperature, with an explicit spherical-normalization correction. We formulate skew query-side score calibration as a strictly convex moment problem and derive a unique normal equation, residual-based optimization certificates, and bounded low-rank projections. A norm-aware margin objective calibrates native squared-distance rankings. Experiments use semantic retrieval data, one million visual descriptors with three codebook seeds, and a ten-million-vector FAISS IVF-PQ index with recomputed exact cosine ground truth. On SIFT1M, skew margin calibration raises native-L2 hit@10 from 0.8926 to 0.8948; symmetric calibration reaches 0.8996. The ten-million-vector index reaches 0.8827 hit@10 at 0.1794 ms per query in a four-thread batch benchmark, while validation selects no skew update. Exact streamed attention over ten million keys evaluates compressed memory on 1,024 held-out queries. Independent matrix solves, automatic differentiation, finite differences, interval arithmetic, full-flow tests, and nine Rocq-checked algebra lemmas support reproducibility. Directionality alone does not establish retrieval superiority.
comments: 42 pages, 9 figures, 10 tables. Includes mathematical appendices and ancillary reproducibility code

title: Pointwise Ergodic Theorems Along $\lfloor p^c\rfloor$ for Every $c>1$
abstract: Let $c>1$ be noninteger, and let $Λ$ denote the von Mangoldt function. The averages \[ A_N^{c} f(x):=\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^{N} Λ(n)f\bigl(T^{\lfloor n^c\rfloor}x\bigr) \] satisfy the variational estimate \[ \bigl\|\mathcal{V}^r(A_N^{c} f:N\in\mathbb{N})\bigr\|_{L^p(X)} \lesssim_{c,p,r}\|f\|_{L^p(X)} \] for every $1<p<\infty$ and $r>2$, on every $σ$-finite measure-preserving system. In particular, the normalized averages along fractional powers of primes converge almost everywhere. The main arithmetic ingredient is a uniform bound on the correlations of $Λ-1$ with fractional-power exponential phases, yielding arbitrarily large powers of logarithmic gain. We obtain this estimate through short-interval polynomial approximation of the fractional phase and higher-order discorrelation estimates. The same approach yields almost-everywhere convergence to for the Möbius-weighted averages along $\left( \lfloor n^c \rfloor \right)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ throughout $1<p<\infty$.
comments: Lean formalization at https://github.com/anastasiosfragkosmath/Pointwise-Ergodic-Theorems-Along-floor-p-c-Palomar-Submission

title: Edge spectral invariants and second-order Steklov asymptotics for the regular tetrahedron
abstract: We give a two-term Weyl asymptotic for the Steklov spectrum of a solid regular tetrahedron. Its linear coefficient is the total edge length times an explicit, absolutely convergent dihedral invariant. A trace-class difference of massive Neumann-to-Dirichlet operators computes the full invariant, including the continuous spectrum. The main analytic step is a fixed-time cumulative trace comparison between the compact tetrahedron and its exact half-space or dihedral models. Localized Hilbert-Schmidt defects have vanishing high-energy tails; retaining the time factor in Duhamel's formula makes this sufficient for an $o(L)$ cumulative error. A separate trace-class face comparison fixes the model's infinite exterior primitive and permits one observation time independent of the inner collar width. Compact-band Mourre estimates and a harmonic comparison establish immediate reflection/transmission support for incident face waves. Triangular unfolding gives null periodic and dead-end sets for the maximal branching relation. Actual edge-window bounds, adapted conical annuli and an ordered-limit Fourier-Tauberian argument then prove the sharp remainder. The proof treats guided and continuum channels together in the edge trace and requires neither a guided metric graph nor a lower-departure estimate uniform at zero tangential momentum.
comments: 27 pages. The AI system GPT-6 Astra was used in preparing this manuscript; see the disclosure on the first page

title: The Nuclear Dimension of Extensions and Graph $C^*$-Algebras
abstract: We prove that the nuclear dimension of any graph $C^*$-algebra is at most two, and we compute the exact value of the nuclear dimension for a large class of graph $C^*$-algebras. In particular, this class covers all graphs with Condition (K). Our methods --- based on Szabó's recent $KK$-uniqueness theorem --- provide a unified approach to computing the nuclear dimension of various extensions. This includes the nuclear dimension of the Toeplitz algebra (first computed by Brake--Winter) and that of the Cuntz--Toeplitz algebras (first computed by Easo et al).
comments: 46 pages, comments welcome! No LLM's were used at any stage during this project

title: Asymptotically Optimal Weighted Edge Colorings via Local Bin Packing
abstract: We study weighted edge coloring, where each edge of a graph $G$ has a weight in $(0,1]$, and colors are assigned so that the incident weight of each color at every vertex is at most one. The objective is to minimize the number of colors, denoted by $χ'_w(G)$. This generalizes classical edge coloring (all weights are one) and bin packing ($G$ is a star). Two natural lower bounds are the maximum weighted degree $Δ_w(G)$ and the maximum local bin-packing number $\mathrm{bp}(G)$: the maximum, over vertices, of the minimum number of unit bins needed to pack the incident weights. We have $\lceilΔ_w(G)\rceil\le\mathrm{bp}(G)\leχ'_w(G)$. How closely these local lower bounds approximate the global optimum is a longstanding open problem. Our main result establishes an asymptotic weighted analogue of Vizing's theorem: every simple graph admits a coloring using at most $(1+o(1))\mathrm{bp}(G)$ colors. Thus local bin packings can be made globally consistent with asymptotically vanishing relative loss, even in nonbipartite graphs. Our local-to-global rounding framework coordinates feasible local packing distributions into a partial coloring, leaving only $o(\mathrm{bp}(G))$ uncolored weight at every vertex. For bipartite multigraphs, we prove $χ'_w(G)\le(2+o(1))Δ_w(G)$, establishing the Chung--Ross conjecture [SICOMP'91] asymptotically. For loopless multigraphs, we obtain the exact bound $χ'_w(G)\le3\lceilΔ_w(G)\rceil$. Both leading coefficients are optimal, giving weighted analogues of the classical Kőnig--Shannon bounds. Further upper and lower bounds show that the classical factor-$3/2$ separation does not persist with the local bin-packing benchmark. We also disprove the exact weighted-degree conjecture of Feige and Singh [ESA'08]. Our upper bounds have polynomial-time algorithms, and their existence statements are formalized in Lean 4.
comments: 94 pages

title: The Structure of a Non-Isometric Non-Contractive Bijection of a Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Space
abstract: On a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space, every bijective non-contractive self-map has the following structure: the quasi-metric splits as $d = λ^- + D_0$. The invariant limit register $λ^-$ is a quasi-pseudo-metric below $d$ for which the map is an isometry, with totally bounded symmetrization on every orbit, so that the map's rigid shadow is a rotation of a compact monothetic group; the asymmetric limit structure on it, a priori only paratopological, carries the compact topology. The defect $D_0$ lies in a band between a past fee difference and the fee of its source, the fee nondecreasing along orbits and vanishing in the deep past. The defect is zero precisely when the map is an isometry. Deep sources are thus almost rigid: in the deep past the map is an isometry to within any $\varepsilon$, against every target. Every such map that is not an isometry is a toll over its rigid shadow, levied on a forward-invariant zone that sheds into the past. Two further facts are forced: the orbit of the source of any strict pair is infinite and already strict, and the source pays its whole defect on its own backward returns, uniformly on a chain-closed set of displacements. The band is attained at both ends, and beyond it the shape of the defect is not forced: three spirals over the circle show that the toll can depend on the target, that a source carrying a fee can descend for free, and that an ascent can carry defect; no rate of shedding is forced either, and for zone tolls (two-valued descent tolls that are shift-monotone and subadditive along their own routes) the fee reaches zero already at a finite depth, by the ascending chain condition on submonoids of $\mathbb{N}$. The results are machine-checked in Lean, apart from a few statements listed at the end.
comments: 15 pages. Lean 4 verification artifacts (five modules, toolchain pins, SHA-256 manifests; Lean 4.32.0, mathlib v4.32.0) included as ancillary files and archived with the paper at Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23544811. Answers Question 7.6 of the toll-spiral paper (arXiv:2610.13973) structurally

title: Lemmas and Conjectures in Spectral Graph Theory
abstract: The corpus of Elie Duhamel and Tristan Cazenave~\cite{dc} contains $305{,}755$ automatically generated conjectures relating spectral and metric invariants of connected graphs. A pipeline generated with Claude Code (numerical refutation, proof by the SMT solver \textsf{z3} from a library of lemmas, discovery of new lemmas, formalisation in \lean~4/Mathlib) refuted $162{,}964$ conjectures and proved $117{,}390$ without any unproved hypothesis, of which $79{,}505$ are verified end to end in \lean{} for every connected graph. This document collects, with proofs written for mathematicians, the most interesting lemmas that were discovered and proved, the ten most useful lemmas, the ten hardest theorems, simpler proofs of known results (Bollobás--Erdős, Yang--Lu), and the unrefuted conjectures that we find most interesting. All the proofs are gathered in an archive

title: Mixing Time of the Random-Pair Monte Shuffle
abstract: In the random-pair Monte shuffle on $n$ cards, each step chooses two positions independently and uniformly and exchanges their cards with probability $1/2$. The chosen positions are public; the decisions to exchange cards remain hidden. We prove that the mixing time in expected conditional total variation distance is $2n\log n+O(n)$, with an exact leading constant and an $O(n)$ cutoff window. To our knowledge, this is the first public-schedule Monte shuffle whose full-permutation mixing time has been determined up to an additive $O(n)$ term. The upper bound follows by comparing two executions with the same public schedule to a classical random-transposition walk. For the lower bound, we construct a schedule-dependent test function and estimate its variance using a matrix-averaging operator. Combined with the depth bound of Czumaj and Lingas, the mixing estimate gives public switching networks with at most $2n\log n+O(n)$ switches and $O(\log n)$ depth for fixed error and failure probabilities. The author obtained this result through interaction with GPT-6 Astra.

title: The Arc Threshold of the Two-Row Ising Torus: Exact Factorization, an Algebraic Critical Coupling, Uniformity in the Circumference, and the Rate of Convergence
abstract: The Lee-Yang circle theorem places every zero of a ferromagnetic Ising partition polynomial on the unit circle. The arc condition, that every zero lie in the closed left half-plane, turns the circle theorem into a product formula for the characteristic function of the occupation count and makes it usable for local limit theorems. For the two-row periodic Ising torus we give the exact reflection factorization of the row transfer matrix, reduce the crossing at zeta = i to a real cubic, and identify the critical coupling a_c* = 0.8637850566870... as the unique root in (0,1) of an explicit octic. We prove that every a > a_c* satisfies the arc condition simultaneously for all circumferences, that no smaller coupling does, and that the finite thresholds approach a_c* at the rate C/n^2 with an explicit algebraic constant C. The factorization and the 2x2 threshold are formalized in Lean 4 against Mathlib; the zeta = i reduction, uniformity and rate are analysis-level.
comments: 28 pages, 4 figures. Lean 4 formal core; the analytic uniformity and rate arguments are paper-level

title: Friedman--Stanley cofinality without Borel completeness
abstract: Friedman and Stanley asked whether an invariant Borel class of countable structures must be Borel complete whenever every countable level of their hierarchy reduces to it. We construct a counterexample in one fixed countable language. The structural counterexample and its principal supporting results have been formalized in Lean~4 and it is available on github.
comments: 26 pages

title: Polynomial configurations and pointwise averages along Piatetski--Shapiro primes
abstract: For every \(c>1\) sufficiently close to \(1\), we prove that there is \(κ>0\) such that every sufficiently large \(A\subset[N]\) of density at least \((\log N)^{-κ}\) contains \[ x,\ x+(p-1),\ x+(p-1)^2,\ldots,\ x+(p-1)^k, \qquad p=\lfloor n^c\rfloor\in\mathbb P. \] We also prove pointwise almost-everywhere convergence of the corresponding multiple ergodic averages.
comments: 15 pages. An AI-assisted Lean development formalizes the deductions in the paper, conditional on eight explicitly documented families of external results. The development is available at https://github.com/HamedMousaviMath/Lean-Formalization-Polynomial-Configurations-and-Pointwise-Averages-Along-Piatetski--Shapiro-Primes

title: Kaplansky's conjectures fail for torsion-free hyperbolic groups in positive characteristic
abstract: Do Kaplansky's group-ring conjectures hold for torsion-free word-hyperbolic groups? We show that all four fail in positive characteristic. For every prime $p$ there is a finitely presented, torsion-free, word-hyperbolic group $G$ with a finite two-dimensional classifying space and $a,b\in\mathbb{F}_p[G]$ with $ab=1\neq ba$. So, over every field of characteristic $p$, the group algebra of $G$ is not directly finite and has a non-trivial idempotent, zero divisor and unit, and $G$ is neither sofic nor surjunctive. For $p=2$, $G$, $a$ and $b$ come from OpenAI's random construction, and we add that $G$ is hyperbolic with probability $1-o(1)$, as are OpenAI's zero-divisor groups. For odd $p$ the groups are new: they adapt OpenAI's direct-finiteness construction with a signed cancellation, found first by S. V. Ivanov and independently by us, via an exact solution of a colour-balance problem and a Perron certificate. As far as we know, they are the first torsion-free counterexamples to direct finiteness and to the idempotent conjecture in odd characteristic. Hyperbolicity comes from one deterministic criterion: if a labelled graph is pattern-free, the group obtained by coning off its components is aspherical and has a linear isoperimetric inequality. We prove it by running OpenAI's exclusion of reduced spheres on van Kampen discs, an accounting OpenAI used for another complex. For every prime $p$, the existence of $G$, $a$ and $b$ and the failure of all four conjectures are formalized in Lean 4, including existence forms of the random-graph estimates used. In characteristic zero, where the idempotent and direct-finiteness conjectures hold for torsion-free hyperbolic groups, we show that no cancellation built into the vertex types survives the decay estimate that makes the groups torsion-free. OpenAI's characteristic-two counterexample with torsion is a CAT(0) group.
comments: 52 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables. First released on Zenodo on 14 October 2026 (v1.0.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23374264); this is v1.0.3 (all versions: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23374263). Lean 4 formalization of the Main Theorem for every prime p: https://github.com/Apsiape/kaplansky-conjectures-hyperbolic-groups/tree/v1.0.3/lean/KaplanskyLean

title: Asymptotic Optimality of $cμ$-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint
abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference, the process by which a pre-trained model receives an input prompt and generates output tokens sequentially, has become increasingly important with the widespread deployment of LLM-based applications. As inference workloads continue to scale, GPU memory has emerged as a critical bottleneck: the long input prompts and generation sequences common in agentic and reasoning workloads lead to substantial key-value (KV) cache usage. In this paper, we study the resulting online scheduling problem from a queueing perspective. Requests arrive stochastically with heterogeneous prompt and output lengths, undergo prefill and autoregressive decode, and compete for a finite KV-cache capacity. Unlike classical queueing models, the duration of a processing step depends on both prefill computation and KV-cache I/O, so service capacity is jointly determined by computation, memory access, and memory occupancy. We develop a fluid model that reduces the system to a multiclass single-server queue with effective service rates capturing computation, memory access, and memory capacity. This fluid analysis yields a $cμ$ priority rule, where the effective service rate $μ$ is jointly determined by computational speed, memory bandwidth, and memory capacity. We prove that this rule minimizes cumulative holding cost in the fluid model and, for a finite workload, also minimizes completion time and maximizes full-run output-token throughput. We then construct a feasible scheduling policy for the original finite system and prove that its scaled dynamics converge to the optimal fluid policy. Finally, experiments on a real LLM serving engine using an NVIDIA H800 show that practical implementations of the proposed priority rule substantially reduce average latency while maintaining high throughput relative to existing scheduling policies.

title: Pseudo-Einstein Structures on Links of Isolated Singularities
abstract: We study Jack Lee's conjecture that, for a compact strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold $M$, the condition $c_1(T^{1,0}M)=0$ in $H^2(M,\mathbb{R})$ implies the existence of a pseudo-Einstein structure. For links of isolated singularities, we construct counterexamples in every odd dimension at least three, with $c_1(T^{1,0}M)=0$ in $H^2(M,\mathbb{Z})$ and $b_1(M)=0$. For isolated algebraic singularities of log canonical type and complex dimension at least three, we prove that the real Chern class condition is equivalent to $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartierness of the canonical divisor, log canonicity, and the existence of a pseudo-Einstein structure. Finally, we construct a Du Bois threefold singularity whose link satisfies the real Chern class condition but admits no pseudo-Einstein structure. The initial versions of the proofs were generated with AI assistance and were subsequently revised and verified by the authors.
comments: 25 pages

title: Path Decompositions of Sparse Graphs via Gaussian Sweeps and Faster Exponential Algorithms
abstract: Using the bisection bound of Monien and Preis, Fomin and Høie proved in 2006 that every graph of maximum degree 3 on $n$ vertices has pathwidth at most $n/6+o(n)$. We prove that the pathwidth, bisection width and cutwidth of these graphs are at most $c_3 n+o(n)$, where $c_3=\frac{3}{4π}\arccos\frac56\approx0.1398$. For bisection width this improves the bound $n/6+o(n)$ of Monien and Preis (2006) and extends to all such graphs the bound that Lichev and Mitsche (2023) obtained for random cubic graphs. For maximum degree 4, we prove that bisection width and cutwidth are at most $n/3+o(n)$, improving the bound $2n/5+o(n)$ of Monien and Preis for 4-regular graphs, and that pathwidth is at most $0.2458n$, improving the bound $n/3$ of Fomin, Gaspers, Saurabh and Stepanov (2009). We show that every graph with $m$ edges has pathwidth at most $7m/48+o(n)$, improving the bound $13m/75$ of Scott and Sorkin (2007), and we give further bounds of the form $\sum_{d\ge3}a_d n_d+o(n)$ with $a_d<1$, where $n_d$ is the number of vertices of degree $d$. The path decompositions, and linear orderings of the stated cutwidth, can be computed in polynomial time. Instead of deriving pathwidth bounds from bisection width, we give each vertex a Gaussian label, a weighted sum of independent standard normal variables over a ball around it, and sweep a threshold through the labels; the bags are frontiers, the vertices above the threshold with a neighbor below it. We bound the probability that a vertex lies in a frontier by comparison with an explicit Gaussian model of a vertex and its neighbors. Faster exact algorithms follow: for feedback vertex set and the traveling salesperson problem on graphs of bounded maximum or average degree, and on general graphs for minimum weight dominating set (by branching until the instance is sparse), Max 2-CSP and counting subgraphs with $k$ edges (by the bound in $m$).
comments: Code, computer certificates and Lean 4 formal proofs: https://serggasp.github.io/pathwidth-site/ and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23883489

title: Conjugator length of Bestvina-Brady groups
abstract: We classify the conjugator length functions of Bestvina-Brady groups. We show that the conjugator length function, when non-trivial, grows as a linear or quadratic polynomial. In fact, we give explicit criteria on the defining graph to determine the precise degree of the polynomial. The proof generalises ideas of Bridson, Riley, and Sale by exploiting the framework developed by Chang and the authors to classify the Dehn functions of Bestvina-Brady groups.
comments: 14 pages, 1 figure. Comments welcome! No AI tools were used for this project

title: Near linear mixing of random-cluster Glauber dynamics on random regular graphs
abstract: We study the random-cluster model on locally treelike graphs at low temperatures. This is a model of dependent percolation parametrized by an edge probability $p \in (0,1)$ and a clustering weight $q \in [1,\infty)$, generalizing independent Bernoulli percolation ($q=1$) and closely related to the classical ferromagnetic Ising and Potts spin systems at integer $q$. For $q>2$, at parameter $p$ below the tree uniqueness threshold $p_{\mathsf u}(q,d)$, it is expected that sampling is easy and local Markov chains mix rapidly on all graphs with degree bounded by $d$. On typical graphs, the same is predicted at $p>p_{\mathsf s}(q,d)$, where $p_{\mathsf s}(q,d)$ is a second uniqueness transition point on the $d$-regular wired tree. Our result confirms this prediction for random regular graphs, showing that the random-cluster Glauber dynamics mix in time $O(n^{1+o(1)})$ on a random $d$-regular graph for all fixed $q>2$ and $p>p_{\mathsf s}$. For comparison, the best prior sampling results for these models that held for all $p>p_{\mathsf s}$ required $q\gtrsim \log d$ \cite{BGPZ26}. The key difficulty is that simply utilizing the contraction of cavity messages on $d$-regular trees does not suffice to cover the entire regime $q>2$. To address this issue, motivated by \cite{LS26}, we develop a careful bootstrap argument to show the shrinkage of disagreement under grand coupling. The core ideas of the proof were generated using GPT-6 and the Pharos system; the proof was then refined and simplified by the author.
comments: 37 pages

title: Pathwise-Budgeted LLM Routing: Online Allocation with K-Bit Tail-Cost Learning
abstract: Firms using large language models under fixed budgets must decide which model to call and whether to retry a failed task. Because a call's charge is revealed only after completion, one long response can exhaust the remaining budget and leave later tasks unserved. Our objective is to maximize the number of tasks solved before service stops. We develop a contextual bandit policy, ADP-HT, which learns each model's task-specific success probability and constructs conservative cost estimates from coarsened response-length labels on a quantile grid with $2^K$ intervals. The policy weighs predicted success against these costs, adjusting the cost penalty to realized spending and the budget available per remaining task. Under calibration, local regularity, and grid-coverage conditions, we bound the excess allowance in the policy's conservative cost estimates. At a fixed sample size, increasing $K$ reduces the discretization term but increases the estimation allowance. At the tightest tested budgets, ADP-HT solves more than twice as many MATH500 and GPQA tasks as the best implemented baseline. It achieves the highest mean cumulative score at ten of fourteen RouterBench budgets. On LiveCodeBench, it outperforms a deployed commercial router in both default and cost-saving modes at the three lowest test budgets.

title: The Invocation Bottleneck in LLM-Based Lossless Compression: What Can Be Removed and What Must Be Traded
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) compress text far better than classical compressors, but LLM-based compressors are slow, particularly during decompression. We argue that their decoding time has two fundamentally different sources. Execution redundancy, such as per-token host transfers, CPU-side coding, and token-by-token encoding, is work that the coded output does not require and can be removed without changing a single output bit. Sequential dependency, one model call per decoded token, is inherent to lossless decoding and cannot be removed by better execution, only traded for more calls or for more bits. We remove execution redundancy with a GPU-resident pipeline whose block-parallel encoding is made lossless in half precision by batch-invariant kernels, speeding up arithmetic coding by up to 5.8x in encoding and 3.0x in decoding without changing its compression rate. We then study the two ways of trading sequential dependency, speculative dual-model coding (SDMC) and multi-token single-model coding (MSMC), characterize the compression cost of predicting several tokens from a shared prefix, and identify the workloads in which fewer model calls are worth that cost.
comments: 14 pages, 7 figures, 4 tables. Code: https://github.com/Angie-Yan/LLM-based-Data-Compression

title: How Unbalanced Must a Latin Rectangle Be?
abstract: We view a $k\times n$ Latin rectangle as $n$ points in the grid $[n]^k$. Each symbol gives one point, whose coordinates are the columns it occupies. The rectangle is balanced when these points are pairwise equidistant in the $\ell_1$ metric. Its imbalance measures the distance from this ideal. We study the minimum imbalance from three sides. Constructively, we use a simulated annealing that moves symbols within rows and only penalises column clashes. Against the reference table of Voboril et al. (2025), it improves 33 of the 51 non-square values for $8\le n\le 13$, by up to 39.4%, and matches the rest. A cheap invariant, the row group, certifies that none of the 33 new rectangles is isotopic to rows of a group table, so the earlier column-swapping local search cannot reach any of them. Exactly, a computer-assisted branch and bound proves that the minimum imbalance of a $3\times 9$ rectangle is $56$. Díaz et al. found this value, but its optimality was open. A sharper pruning bound, derived from the identity $I=2\sum(d-t)^+$, reduces the search tree by a factor of $2.4$ to $3.3$ on the instances with $k\ge3$ that we solve. Asymptotically, the minimum imbalance is $Θ(n^3)$ for every fixed $k$. A pigeonhole argument gives a lower constant of order $k\,4^{-k}$, and random rectangles give an upper constant of order $\sqrt k$. For $k=2$, the limit of $\min I/n^3$ exists, a permuton attains it, and it lies between $4/375$ and $0.1196$. Perfect balance is an $\ell_1$-equilateral problem, so it forces $k=Ω(n/\log n)$ rows. For $2\times n$ rectangles, single two-minute annealing runs improve five of the seven six-hour MIP upper bounds for $14\le n\le 20$. Finally, the Lean 4 kernel checks every rectangle reported in this paper against a 74-line specification that imports only Lean's core library. We also prove the pigeonhole lower bound in Lean with Mathlib.

title: Representation embeddings and the third Brauer--Thrall conjecture
abstract: Let $A$ be a representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field $k$. We prove that for every infinite cardinal $κ$ there is an indecomposable $A$-module $M$ with $\dim_k M=κ$. Over algebraically closed fields, this settles Simson's conjecture, also called the third Brauer--Thrall conjecture, that every representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra has indecomposable modules of arbitrarily large cardinality. To construct these modules, we extend Bongartz's representation embedding from finite-dimensional Kronecker modules without a simple injective summand to such modules of arbitrary dimension. The extended functor commutes with direct sums and filtered colimits and preserves the dimension of infinite-dimensional modules. Applying it to the indecomposable Kronecker modules of every infinite dimension constructed by Göbel and Simson yields the required $A$-modules.
comments: 24 pages, comments welcome! full Lean formalization of main results are available at https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/third-brauer-thrall-conjecture

title: From hydrological laws to catchment models: A process-based model matches deep-learning accuracy on three continents
abstract: Dooge asked whether hydrology has laws at the catchment scale. We ask whether a low-dimensional system built under physical laws can match the accuracy of neural networks that outperform process-based models on the same inputs. Three laws constrain a lumped catchment model. Conservation makes it a flux-connected storage network, dissipation fixes the sign of every flux and aggregation determines how the unresolved composition enters the fluxes, through effective laws over threshold distributions and a memory of the forcing. These laws admit four kinds of refinement. A parsimonious model under them, CaRT (11 parameters per catchment), is refined in a loop assisted by AI agents. Each refinement addresses an observed deficit through a hypothesis from the literature. The result, CaRT+, has fourteen states, 35 parameters per catchment and no daily neural network. Most refinements follow from aggregation over thresholds or from variables that carry no water but modulate fluxes. On 602 British and 593 US gauged catchments, single CaRT+ models reach median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiencies of 0.863 and 0.765 in held-out years. A stateful LSTM reaches 0.869 and 0.751 and an entity-aware LSTM 0.862 and 0.754, while three-seed LSTM ensembles remain ahead of the CaRT+ ensemble by 0.003-0.012 in median paired NSE. On 505 drier Australian gauged catchments unused in development, single CaRT+ models reach 0.778 against 0.762 and 0.753 for the two LSTMs. The results suggest that catchment-scale laws exist as laws of form, with the constitutive families shared and only their parameters learned.
comments: 61 pages, 12 figures, 13 tables, plus 19 pages of Supporting Information

title: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
abstract: We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^\natural$ and formalizes Zhu's modular invariance, Huang's tensor categories with the Verlinde formula, the Gannon-Rayhaun classification of $c=1$ VOAs, and classical freeness of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ (Arakawa-Dai) and of the minimal models $M(2,2m+3)$ (van Ekeren-Heluani). It also contains new results: graded first-order rigidity of all Virasoro minimal models and of $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at every admissible level; classical freeness of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, and of the other members of the Deligne series under stated assumptions; and a proof that graded unitarity of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ implies that of the minimal models $M(2,2n+1)$. The library declares no axiom of its own.
comments: 5 pages. Lean library, book and short version: https://github.com/Fedor-Popov/Lean_VOA (release v1.0)

title: Polynomial-Time Differentially Private Synthetic Graph Release with Nearly-Linear Additive Error
abstract: We give a polynomial-time $(\varepsilon, δ)$-edge-differentially private algorithm that releases a synthetic graph approximately preserving all cut values of a nonnegative weighted input graph $G$. Our algorithm outputs a nonnegative weighted graph $H$ such that, with probability at least $1-β$, simultaneously for all $S\subseteq V$, \[ \left|w_G(S,V\setminus S)-w_H(S,V\setminus S)\right| \leq γw_G(S,V\setminus S) + O\left(\frac{n}{γ\varepsilon} \log^7 \frac{n}{δβγ\varepsilon}\right). \] For fixed $γ, \varepsilon$ and $δ= β= n^{-10}$, the additive error is $n \operatorname{polylog} n$, improving upon the previous efficient bound of $n^{13/12 + o(1)}$. Furthermore, we establish an $Ω(n/γ\varepsilon)$ lower bound for the relevant parameter regime, showing that our result is tight up to polylogarithmic factors. Our algorithm uses a log-det-regularized SDP to generate fractional queries for multiplicative-weights updates and certify accuracy for all cuts. The privacy analysis charges privacy loss only fractionally per mechanism call, based on the amount of mass on edge coordinates retired from subsequent iterations. Our synthetic graph release yields improved error bounds for several downstream tasks in private graph analysis including correlation clustering, Max-Cut, Max-$k$-Cut, constrained cut problems and hierarchical clustering. Most notably, for unweighted complete-graph correlation clustering, we achieve the optimal $\widetilde O(n)$ additive error while reducing the best previously known approximation ratio for this additive error from several thousand to $1.387$. We also provide a formalization of our results in Lean.
